observation.visible_scene: A frosty canal on a clear, partly cloudy morning. A snow/frost-covered towpath runs along the left bank; the right bank is lined with several moored narrowboats (a cream-and-blue covered boat, a dark-hulled boat, and a grey boat with an orange panel), all mirrored in the still water. A large green hedge and bare trees sit behind the boats. Far down the canal on the left, a dark narrowboat faces the camera with a thin plume of smoke/steam rising from its chimney. A faint aircraft contrail crosses the upper sky. The camera viewpoint is fixed throughout.
visible_changes: The smoke/steam plume from the distant boat's chimney is continuously emitted and drifts leftward, its shape and extent changing from frame to frame (the only clearly ongoing process).
The distant dark boat remains in essentially the same position relative to the bank and its own reflection across the segment; any forward motion is at most very slight and not clearly resolved.
The water surface and the boat/tree reflections stay largely stable, with only minor shimmer/ripple variation.
The contrail in the sky persists as a thin diagonal streak with no obvious large movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the distant boat is moored or slowly underway (the segment does not settle this).
The cause of the smoke (engine/heating) and any later change in its intensity or direction.
Events before the crop boundary (onset of the smoke) and after it (continuation or cessation).
uncertain_details: Exact position change of the distant boat between first and last frames is too small to confirm as motion vs. static.
Slow drift of the contrail, if any, is not clearly measurable.
Subtle ripple changes in the reflections cannot be attributed to a specific cause.
